chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

You should say during the last ten days of the month of Ramadan, every night: 'I seek refuge in the Majesty of Your Noble Face lest the month of Ramadan pass me by, or dawn rise from this night of mine, while You have a sin or a debt against me for which You will punish me.'
ai.seo_question: What is the recommended supplication to recite during the last ten nights of Ramadan?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Kafi, this supplication emphasizes the anxiety of the believer regarding unexpiated sins or debts (tabi'ah) that might hinder acceptance of worship during the final nights. It reflects the Shia tradition of intense self-accountability (muhasabah) and the hope for divine mercy as Ramadan concludes, ensuring one enters Shawwal with a clean spiritual slate.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from one of our companions, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘You should be saying during the last ten (days) from a Month of Ramazan, during each night, ‘I hereby seek Refuge with the Majesty of Your<sup>azwj</sup> Benevolent Face that You<sup>azwj</sup> Expire from me the Month of Ramazan, or Emerge the day from this night of mine, before I sin, or something which would be followed by you<sup>azwj</sup> Punishing me’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from certain individuals of our people who has said the following: “Abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that during the last ten nights of the month of Ramadan, you should say the following prayer.

‘O Allah, I seek refuge with the glory of Your honorable face against the condition in which the month of Ramadan will pass or this night will dawn while I may have committed sins or such deeds for which I will deserve your punishment.’”
